newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Oppn pressures Howard on probe.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Oppn pressures Howard on probe.

text.p: The Australian Opposition attempted on Thursday to force Prime Minister John Howard to account in parliament for his statements on an investigation into retiring senator Bob Woods.
Opposition Leader Kim Beazley wanted to move in the House of Representatives that Howard come into the lower house and correct his alleged misleading of the public earlier this week.
The government, with its preponderant numbers in the house, refused to let Beazley even put put the motion.
The Australian Federal Police are investigating Woods, a junior member of the government who said on Monday he was quitting parliament, for allegedly dishonest expenses claims.
On Tuesday, a television interviewer asked Howard when Woods had first advised him of this.
Howard said Woods had told him 10 days before.
But the government's Senate Leader, Robert Hill, told the Senate on Wednesday that Attorney-General Daryl Williams had advised Howard of the investigation late last year.

The opposition says this means that, while Howard may have been telling the truth in saying when Woods told him about the investigation, he was misleading the public by not adding that he had known about it since late last year.
